title: Give advice and explore hypothetical choices
lessons:
## What you will learn to communicate
Make a polite request, give advice without issuing an order, explore an imagined choice, and explain how a past result could have been different. You will compare solutions and respond to an unexpected constraint rather than memorize a speech. These are learning tasks, not calibrated TCF items.

## Before you start
Retrieve Chapter 13 future stems, Chapter 11 imparfait endings and Chapter 12 plus-que-parfait. Check: `je pourrai` — I will be able to; `j'avais` — I had/was having; `j'avais réservé` — I had booked. The conditional combines familiar components, but its meaning is not simply future time. If these forms are unclear, practise six useful verbs before continuing.

## 1. Form the conditionnel présent
Use the futur simple stem plus imparfait endings: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. `Je parlerais, tu parlerais, elle parlerait, nous parlerions, vous parleriez, ils parleraient` — I would speak, you would speak… . For most -er/-ir verbs, use the infinitive; for many -re verbs, remove the final e: `je choisirais` — I would choose; `nous attendrions` — we would wait. Irregular future stems remain irregular: `je serais` — I would be; `j'aurais` — I would have; `j'irais` — I would go; `je ferais` — I would do; `je viendrais` — I would come; `je pourrais` — I could/would be able to; `je voudrais` — I would like; `je devrais` — I should/would have to; `je saurais` — I would know; `j'enverrais` — I would send; `il faudrait` — it would be necessary.

Compare `je pourrai` — I will be able to, a future statement, with `je pourrais` — I could, a possibility or hypothetical ability. Final -ai and -ais may sound different depending on accent, but the distinction is not always audible. Use context and spelling, not only vowel imitation. Nous/vous forms provide clearer contrasts: pourrons/pourrions, pourrez/pourriez.

## 2. Politeness and advice
`Je voudrais déplacer mon rendez-vous.` — I would like to move my appointment. `Pourriez-vous vérifier la facture ?` — Could you check the bill? `Est-ce qu'il serait possible de payer en deux fois ?` — Would it be possible to pay in two instalments? An explicit si clause is not required for these polite uses. A request remains more considerate when it includes a reason and allows a response; the conditional is not a magic politeness switch.

For advice, use `Vous devriez demander un devis.` — You should request a quotation. `À ta place, je comparerais les garanties.` — In your position, I would compare the warranties. `Il vaudrait mieux attendre.` — It would be better to wait. Distinguish advice from obligation: `Vous devez présenter une pièce d'identité.` — You must show identification, states a requirement; `Vous devriez apporter une copie.` — You should bring a copy, recommends a precaution. In ordinary French, pourrais does not always translate English could in the past: `Quand j'étais enfant, je pouvais nager longtemps.` — As a child, I could swim for a long time, is past ability and uses imparfait.

## 3. Three practical si patterns
A real/open condition uses si + present, followed by future, present or imperative: `Si le magasin est ouvert, j'irai ce soir.` — If the shop is open, I will go tonight. `Si tu as un doute, appelle.` — If you are unsure, call. A hypothetical present/future condition uses si + imparfait, followed by present conditional: `Si j'avais plus de temps, je suivrais ce cours.` — If I had more time, I would take this course. This does not necessarily refer to past time; avais marks the imagined condition.

An unreal past condition uses si + plus-que-parfait, followed by past conditional: `Si j'avais vérifié l'adresse, je ne me serais pas perdu.` — If I had checked the address, I would not have got lost, said by a male speaker. The condition was not met and the past result cannot now be changed. Do not use conditional immediately after conditional si: not si j'aurais le temps in the standard hypothetical pattern. English if I would is not a template for French. However, si can mean whether after a verb of questioning: `Je voudrais savoir si vous pourriez venir.` — I would like to know whether you could come. That is an indirect question, not the conditional if-clause rule.

## 4. Form and use the conditionnel passé
Use present conditional avoir or être plus a participle: `J'aurais accepté.` — I would have accepted. `Elle serait venue.` — She would have come. `Nous nous serions inscrits.` — We would have registered. Apply the same agreement rules as other compound tenses: ordinary être agrees with subject, avoir with a preceding direct object, and pronominals depend on object function. `Elle se serait lavé les mains.` — She would have washed her hands. `Les dates que j'aurais choisies…` — The dates I would have chosen… . Negation surrounds the auxiliary: `Je n'aurais pas payé sans reçu.` — I would not have paid without a receipt.

Use the past conditional for a missed opportunity or criticism with care: `J'aurais dû demander de l'aide.` — I should have asked for help. `Tu aurais pu me prévenir.` — You could have warned me. The second can sound reproachful; choose tone and purpose consciously. A useful mixed timeline links an earlier unreal cause to a present result: `Si j'avais pris ce poste, j'habiterais plus près d'ici.` — If I had taken that job, I would live nearer here now. Learn this only after the three core patterns are secure. Journalists also use conditional for unconfirmed reports; recognize it without treating an allegation as fact, but production here focuses on advice and hypotheses.

## 5. Pronunciation, chunks and English traps
Speak `pourriez-vous` in one polite group, then pause before the request. In `j'aurais aimé`, link the s with the following vowel. Compare `je voudrais` — I would like, and `je voulais` — I wanted; the r is meaningful. Avoid translating I would go every summer automatically with conditional: if English would means a past habit, use `J'y allais chaque été.` — I used to go there every summer. Browser speech is synthetic; use it for phrase practice, not as proof of authentic-listening readiness.

## 6. Try, then reveal
A. Politely request an estimate. B. Imagine more money and a different housing choice. C. Regret not checking the timetable. D. Explain why si j'aurais is wrong in a hypothetical if clause but possible after I wonder whether.

:::answer
A. `Pourriez-vous m'envoyer un devis ?` — Could you send me an estimate? B. `Si j'avais plus d'argent, je choisirais un logement plus proche.` — If I had more money, I would choose a nearer home. C. `Si j'avais vérifié l'horaire, je n'aurais pas manqué le départ.` — If I had checked the timetable, I would not have missed departure. Also: `J'aurais dû vérifier l'horaire.` — I should have checked the timetable. D. Conditional si takes the appropriate present/imparfait/plus-que-parfait pattern, but si meaning whether introduces an indirect question: `Je me demande si j'aurais assez de temps.` — I wonder whether I would have enough time.
:::

## 7. Integrated transfer and spaced retrieval
Listen for whether the choice is real, imagined or a past regret. Read for the writer's intended advice, not just the word si. Speak to solve a fresh problem and react to its constraint. Write a supportive message, not a list of criticisms. Recycle comparison, past causes and future planning. Divide bank 001–100 into four sets. A four-hour session can use 35 minutes retrieval, 45 listening, 40 reading, 45 speaking, 45 writing and 30 corrections. Revisit after one day, three days, seven days and two weeks. Log the condition's time and reality status before correcting the form. If patterns blur, label three timelines and make one meaningful example for each. Keep self-assessment separate from objective results; neither establishes an official level.

activities.title: Advice, not a requirement
activities.prompt: Which suggestion does the adviser make?
activities.script: Tu hésites entre acheter ce vélo et réparer l'ancien ? À ta place, je demanderais d'abord un devis. Si la réparation coûtait moins de cent dollars, je garderais l'ancien vélo. En revanche, si le cadre est cassé, n'attends pas pour demander un avis professionnel. Je ne choisirais pas seulement selon la couleur du modèle neuf.
options: Buy the new bicycle for its colour.
Repair it regardless of its condition.
Ask for a repair estimate before deciding.
activities.explanation: The first recommendation is to get a quotation. Keeping the old bicycle is hypothetical and depends on cost; a broken frame calls for professional assessment.

activities.title: A missed opportunity
activities.prompt: What actually happened, according to the speaker?
activities.script: J'aurais participé à l'atelier si j'avais vu l'annonce plus tôt. Quand je l'ai découverte, les inscriptions étaient closes. J'ai quand même écrit à l'organisatrice. Elle m'a proposé une liste d'attente, mais personne ne s'est désisté. La prochaine fois, je consulterai le programme dès sa publication.
options: The speaker attended after someone cancelled.
The speaker missed registration and did not attend.
activities.explanation: The past conditional describes unrealized participation. Registration had closed, and the waiting list produced no place.

activities.title: A supportive response
activities.prompt: What is the writer's main proposal?
activities.passage: Tu dis que tes trajets te fatiguent. Je ne quitterais pas ton poste immédiatement. Si ton responsable acceptait un jour de télétravail, tu pourrais tester cette organisation pendant un mois. Si cela ne suffit pas, il serait alors raisonnable de chercher plus près. Tu aurais peut-être dû en parler avant, mais l'important est de trouver une solution maintenant.
options: Try a limited remote-working arrangement before a larger decision.
activities.explanation: The writer proposes a reversible trial, subject to the manager's agreement. The past regret is secondary, not the proposed solution.

activities.title: Understand the condition
activities.prompt: Which conclusion follows from the message?
activities.passage: Si nous avions confirmé la salle vendredi, nous aurions bénéficié du tarif réduit. Nous avons attendu lundi et le tarif normal s'applique maintenant. Pour une prochaine réservation, je proposerais de fixer une date de décision commune. Si vous êtes d'accord, je préparerai un calendrier demain.
options: The group missed the discount by confirming too late.
The writer has already prepared tomorrow's calendar.
The room was unavailable on Friday.
activities.explanation: The unmet Friday confirmation condition explains the lost discount. The calendar is a future action conditional on agreement; room availability is not discussed.

activities.title: Advise without dictating
activities.prompt: A friend is considering a long commute for a better-paid job. Ask two questions, compare priorities, offer two conditional suggestions, and mention a past mistake that could inform the choice. Halfway through, imagine the friend says: Remote work is impossible. Adapt rather than repeat.
activities.model: Quelle est la durée exacte du trajet ? Et combien coûterait le transport chaque mois ? À ta place, je calculerais le gain réel après les frais. Si l'entreprise acceptait un horaire décalé, tu éviterais peut-être les heures de pointe. Le télétravail est impossible ? Alors, je demanderais plutôt si tu peux regrouper tes heures sur quatre jours. Pour mon ancien poste, j'aurais dû tester le trajet avant de signer. Si j'avais fait cet essai, j'aurais mieux compris la fatigue quotidienne. Je te conseille donc de faire le parcours un matin de semaine.
rubric: Fulfillment: questions, priorities, suggestions and a relevant past lesson.
Interaction: adapts to the no-remote-work constraint.
Coherence: advice follows from costs and daily needs.
Range/control: distinguishes real conditions, hypothetical advice and past regret.
Intelligibility/register: supportive tone, clear speech, no claim that advice is compulsory.

activities.title: Propose an alternative arrangement
activities.prompt: Write 110–150 words to an association after an invented scheduling problem. Make a polite request, explain what would help now, mention one earlier action that would have prevented the problem, and suggest an open-condition next step. Be constructive, not accusatory.
activities.model:
Bonjour,
Je participe à votre atelier du mercredi, mais mon nouvel horaire de travail m'empêche d'arriver à temps. Serait-il possible de rejoindre le groupe du samedi ? Si une place était disponible, je pourrais terminer la formation sans manquer de séance. J'aurais dû vous prévenir dès l'annonce de mon changement d'horaire ; je regrette ce retard. Si j'avais vérifié mon calendrier plus tôt, j'aurais demandé le transfert avant le début du cycle. Pour l'instant, je préférerais une solution qui conserve mon inscription plutôt qu'un remboursement. Si vous êtes d'accord, je vous enverrai demain mes disponibilités précises. Je reste joignable par téléphone chaque matin. Merci de m'indiquer les possibilités et les éventuels frais de modification.
Cordialement,
Éric
rubric: Fulfillment: polite request, present hypothetical benefit, past prevention and next step.
Organization: problem, alternatives and action are easy to locate.
Range: advice/request chunks and varied conditional patterns.
Control: avoids conditional after conditional si; checks compound auxiliaries.
Register: constructive responsibility-taking, appropriate greeting and closing.
